title: “I want 100% recycled packaging, but I want it in a plastic-sealed carton!”: implementing sustainability in an emerging market
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: Purpose This research examines how young consumers in an emerging market make trade-off decisions when buying products on e-commerce platforms. It specifically investigates how different types of online shops and sustainable packaging influence these choices. Design/methodology/approach A choice-based conjoint analysis was conducted to study consumer preferences for multi-attribute products with 133 young Thai consumers. The product profiles varied across attributes such as shop type, inner and secondary packaging, and price. The analysis used part-worth utility, marginal willingness to pay and market simulations to test the hypotheses. Findings The results confirmed that consumers prefer to buy from official shops, which they perceive as trustworthy. While they prefer 100% recycled plastic inner packaging, they are not willing to pay extra for it. Conversely, consumers prefer and are willing to pay a premium for secondary packaging with a plastic seal, as it signals authenticity and safety. When buying from an official shop, consumers are more likely to choose products without secondary packaging, as the shop’s reputation reduces their concerns about counterfeit products. Originality/value This research highlights how the risk of counterfeit products in emerging markets acts as a barrier to sustainable consumption. It shows that consumers prioritize personal safety over sustainability. The findings, supported by signaling theory and psychological egoism, contribute to a better understanding of green consumption behavior in these unique contexts.

title: Wintertime organic carbon export provides a potential food source for zooplankton in the High Arctic
abstract: Abstract Pulsed particulate organic carbon export plays a vital role in sustaining Arctic marine ecosystems and the biological pump. Wintertime particulate organic carbon export in ice-covered Arctic waters is generally considered negligible due to light-limited local primary production. However, using time-series sediment-trap samples, we observe a high wintertime particulate organic carbon flux lasting over three months at the ice-covered Northwind Abyssal Plain in the High Arctic. We examine its drivers and implications for zooplankton. Here, we show that elevated particulate organic carbon fluxes during winter coincide with increased fecal-pellet carbon and zooplankton swimmer fluxes. Fecal-pellet evidence and nitrogen isotope values indicate that the wintertime carbon export represents a potential food source for zooplankton during the dark season. This wintertime carbon flux is consistent with lateral input, plausibly sourced from shelf and slope regions. Our results demonstrate that such wintertime carbon export provides an important food source for overwintering zooplankton, highlighting its ecological role in ice-covered Arctic ecosystems.

title: Unified definition of integrated diagnostics: a position statement of the EFLM
abstract: Abstract Integrated diagnostics is an emerging multidisciplinary model of care that integrates traditionally siloed domains, including pathology, radiology, genomics, and laboratory medicine, into a coordinated framework designed to improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment selection, and clinical outcomes. In this position statement, the EFLM Integrated Diagnostics Committee proposes a concise and operational definition of integrated diagnostics and outlines the relevance for healthcare systems. Integrated diagnostics has the potential to advance precision medicine through improved data integration, more coordinated interpretation, and enhanced clinical decision-making. Drawing on multidisciplinary expert consensus, we recommend adoption of a standardized conceptual framework to support research, clinical implementation, interoperability, and policy development across healthcare systems with implementation adapted to local needs, scale, and digital maturity.

Tumor-infiltrating B cells evolve towards interferon-rich trajectories aligned with immunotherapy in melanoma
journal: Journal of Experimental & Clinical Cancer Research
abstract: Abstract Background B cells are increasingly recognized regulators of antitumor immunity in melanoma, yet their differentiation states, lineage dynamics, spatial organization and integration within the immune microenvironment, and how these are influenced with immunotherapy remain incompletely defined. Methods We conducted deep profiling of tumor-resident B cell differentiation and evolutionary features in the melanoma tumor microenvironment using bulk, single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses, long-read antibody sequencing and mass cytometry (Cytometry by Time-Of-Flight, CyTOF). We characterized B cell differentiation trajectories, class-switching patterns, antibody isotype usage, signaling pathways, spatial niches against clinicopathological features and immune cell communication, before and after checkpoint blockade and in clinically defined responders and non-responders. Results Melanoma-infiltrating B cells were enriched across primary and metastatic lesions, were preferentially associated with immune-rich tumors and correlated with T and natural killer (NK) cell densities. Long-read immunoglobulin sequencing demonstrated recurrent class switch recombination (CSR) trajectories with predominant IgG and IgA isotype usage, confirmed by bulk transcriptomic analyses. Across independent single-cell and bulk transcriptomic datasets we identified conserved class-switching, B cell receptor (BCR) activation, and pseudotime analyses showed differentiation trajectories progressing from naïve and memory states toward interferon (IFN)-driven terminal differentiation trajectories that persisted before and after immunotherapy. CyTOF analyses independently confirmed proliferative, germinal center (GC)-like, memory and class-switched B cell subsets, suggesting conserved inflammatory differentiation endpoints. Spatial transcriptomic deconvolution identified IFN-rich B cells within tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS). Following immunotherapy, B cells retained class-switched trajectories, displayed enriched GC-associated profiles, enhanced crosstalk with T cells and Dendritic Cells (DCs) and preserved or induced IFN-rich IgM + /IgD + or IgG4 + phenotypes, suggesting persistence or emergence of non-class switched and atypical class-switched isotype profiles. Transcriptomic analyses of B cells pointed to upregulated antigen-driven stimulation and BCR signaling, whereas in non-responders displayed IFN-rich B cells, IFN-associated genes, and IFN-pathway enrichment. Conclusions Melanoma-infiltrating B cells follow class-switched differentiation trajectories culminating in IFN signaling, atypical antibody expressing states that persist or emerge after immunotherapy, aligning dynamic B cell evolution and atypical lineage traits with immunotherapy.

title: The incidence, pathogen spectrum, and resistance profile of pyogenic spondylodiscitis: A nationwide retrospective evaluation of G-DRG data
The impact of digital supply chain integration on sustainable export performance: the role of sustainable supply chain resilience and supply chain transparency
abstract: Purpose Sustainability and resilience have become critical requirements for maintaining competitiveness in international markets. Yet export-oriented firms still struggle to meet these requirements effectively. While digitally enabled supply chains can potentially help firms in this regard, it remains unclear whether, how and when digital supply chains can contribute to sustainable supply chain resilience (SSCR) and sustainable export performance. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to investigate the impact of digital supply chain integration (DSCI) on sustainable export performance and the mediating role of SSCR and the moderating role of supply chain transparency. Design/methodology/approach The study employs the partial least squares-structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) technique to analyse 242 survey responses obtained from manufacturing firms across different sectors in Jordan. Findings The analysis indicates that DSCI positively influences sustainable export performance both directly and indirectly by enhancing SSCR. However, the analysis reveals that supply chain transparency does not moderate the impact of DSCI on SSCR, suggesting that DSCI drives SSCR regardless of the level of supply chain transparency. Originality/value This study examines the impact of DSCI on sustainable export performance and its underlying mechanism and boundary condition. This enriches the theoretical understanding of whether, how and when DSCI can contribute to sustainable export performance and offers valuable insights for managers aiming to improve sustainable performance in international markets.

title: Scalable Synthesis of a Masked Thiophenol as an Air-Stable, Odorless Intermediate to the Aurora Kinase Inhibitor Tozasertib (VX-680)
abstract: Abstract The use of thiophenols on process scales is fraught with challenges relating to their toxicity, malodor, and air sensitivity. We previously demonstrated that the Ni-catalyzed C–S coupling of aryl iodides and thiourea provides a discovery-scale route to S-aryl isothiouronium salts, which serve as bench stable, odorless, and highly crystalline surrogates of thiophenols. Here, we report the process optimization of this methodology for the synthesis of a key intermediate to kinase inhibitor tozasertib (VX-680). The corollary is a reduction in catalyst loading to 0.5 mol %, elimination of NMP solvent, and introduction of a direct crystallization, giving 95% yield on a 100 g scale.
